text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

* A final agreement to restructure ship repairer Lisnave was signed ysterday by major shareholders and Economy Minister Augusto Mateus. The company has orders worth 16.8 billion escudos, which guarantee its activity for two more years.
* Gas company Lusitaniagas is interested in taking a 10 percent stake in a company that will distribute natural gas in central Portugal.
* TAP pilots and the government are close to an agreement that will allow them to keep talking and avert a further strike over working hours.
* The price of petrol may rise in Portugal from August 7 due to the increase in the dollar and the price of oil in the international market, analysts say.
* Insurance company Imperio may invest between 10 and 24 billion escudos to buy insurance companies in Spain in the medium term, a senior Imperio official told the paper.
* Sales of the three biggest retail groups rose by 7.1 percent in the first semester of 1997 to 388.8 billion escudos, the Portuguese Association of Retail Companies said.

* State airline TAP-Air Portugal, in partnership with Air Madeira, will launch a new company to manage the profitable charter business, which has been seriously affected by the recent TAP pilots' strike.
